checkpoints.description: [1/4] check --push exits 1 when the requested push is skipped or refused; the three dirty-tree tests expect 1; a refused-push test; a test that fix never pushes; ADR-187. [2/4] verify_commit treats a commit any remote-tracking branch contains as pushed; the annotation guard also reads module-level annotations; a guard for f-string syntax Python 3.10 rejects; ADR-188 corrects ADR-181, ADR-182, ADR-186 and three commit messages. [3/4] run_shell refuses NUL; the ledger audit unquotes git's quoted paths; hygiene, update_knowledge_base and verify_commit print UTF-8 on Windows; ADR-189. [4/4] Full re-verification of every commit, then report.

impact_assessment.why: The verification of the nine unpushed commits found nine issues, each reproduced, with every proposed fix tested; the stop hook and the user's standing pattern call for fixing what is found. Re-checking the private-attribute rule showed its 12 production hits in neurocore are the singleton idiom, so widening it would flag correct code and the recommendation is withdrawn.
impact_assessment.benefits: An explicit --push that fails is reported as a failure; the reset advice cannot target a published commit; the 3.10 guards cover module annotations and PEP 701 f-strings; no command crashes on a NUL; ledger reports name real paths, spaces included; project gate output keeps non-ASCII names.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: check --push now exits 1 when its push does not happen; status --json reports unquoted paths; Fix text changes for a pushed commit without upstream. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: A failing-first test per fix; the changed test expectations named in ADR-187 under PRINCIPLE-014 R3; the path unquoting is a pure function tested on git's own quoted output; every commit verified alone.

[1/1] The ledger audit reads git status --porcelain -z, closing ADR-189's limit on renames whose names hold ' -> '; the check --push help and README state the exit-1 behaviour 2f123c0 added, as PRINCIPLE-005 R2 requires; ADR-190.

impact_assessment.why: Reviewing the two changed help forms in full showed check --push's help and README still described the pre-2f123c0 behaviour, although PRINCIPLE-005 R2 requires a change to a command's non-zero exit conditions to update its --help and README in the same commit. ADR-189 left v1 porcelain's rename ambiguity open.
impact_assessment.benefits: The audit parses every path exactly, renames included; check's help and README match what the command does.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: check --help text changes; git_porcelain_status returns NUL-separated output; the rename display stays old -> new. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests on a synthesised -z rename with arrows in its names and on a real git mv through the real audit; v1 parsing kept for callers and tests that pass v1 text.

[1/2] delegate never runs through cmd.exe, ends options before the brief, and checks the model name without its #variant (ADR-194); [2/2] ADR-195 records the push 21-30 review

impact_assessment.why: Pushes 21-30 review: on Windows opencode is an npm .CMD shim, so a brief with a quote and & ran arbitrary commands and %VAR% expanded into the brief; a brief starting with -- was parsed as opencode flags (--auto approves permissions); opencode/<paid>#-free passed the free-model check.
impact_assessment.benefits: No shell interprets a brief; the brief is always the message; only free models run.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a .cmd/.bat opencode whose real executable cannot be found refuses briefs holding cmd metacharacters; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Failing-first tests with a fake shim and a recorded argv; Phase 4 and verify_commit per milestone.
